paragraphs: Here is the big idea, friend: order is not the enemy of God's gifts. Order is how the gifts reach people. Paul says, "All of these must be done to build up the church." (1 Corinthians 14:26) A gift that only puts on a show is like me stamping cookies for an hour and never opening the box.

That's why Paul cares about turns, interpreters and weighing what is said. He wants all of them to prophesy in turn "so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged." (1 Corinthians 14:31) And the reason underneath it all is that God is not a God of disorder, but of peace… (1 Corinthians 14:33) So when you hold back for the sake of someone else, that's love in action, friend.

Paul doesn't tell them to shut the gifts down, either. He says, "be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues." (1 Corinthians 14:39) Then he adds, "But everything must be done in a proper and orderly manner." (1 Corinthians 14:40) So bring what God has given you with ALL your heart, and ask one question first: will this build somebody up? I've asked myself that after a few lopsided cookies, believe me.
